0.0.n: The て-form of 続く introduces the next action in a sequence.

0.2.n: 会社 means a company, but here refers to the speaker’s workplace.

0.3.n: Links 会社 to ほう in a softened way of referring to the workplace.

0.4.n: In 会社のほう, ほう softens the location reference rather than identifying a literal side.

0.5.n: Marks the place where the eating happens.

0.6.n: A neutral word for the morning meal, somewhat more formal than 朝ごはん.

0.7.n: Shows that 朝食 is what the speaker eats.

0.8.n: 食べる in て-form plus いきます politely presents eating as the next action to proceed with.

1.0.n: Refers to the speaker’s own place, not just a house as a building.

1.1.n: Marks home as the location of the eating.

1.2.n: Names the meal being eaten at home.

1.3.n: Marks 朝食 as what is eaten.

1.4.n: The plain form comes before と to describe a general condition.

1.5.n: Presents eating at home as a condition that regularly produces the following result.

1.6.n: This is the thing being used up, marked by が.

1.7.n: Marks 時間 as what undergoes consumption.

1.8.n: Passive form of 消費する: time is used up rather than doing the consuming.

1.9.n: Limits the result to time being used up, implying no added benefit.

1.10.n: The linking form of だ connects だけ to explanatory んです.

1.11.n: Short for の; it presents the statement as background for the speaker’s point.

1.12.n: Adds politeness to the explanation in んです.

1.13.n: Connects this statement to the contrasting advantage described next.

2.0.n: Refers to the workplace where the speaker is employed.

2.1.n: Marks the workplace as the location of the action.

2.2.n: 中 attaches to 仕事 to indicate being in the middle of work.

2.3.n: Marks 仕事中 as the time when the eating happens.

2.4.n: Names the meal eaten during working hours.

2.5.n: Identifies 朝食 as what the speaker eats.

2.6.n: The plain form precedes と to introduce a condition.

2.7.n: Links eating during work to the result of receiving pay.

2.8.n: Usually refers to an hourly wage rate; here it means pay accruing during work time.

2.9.n: Marks 時給 as what arises or accrues.

2.10.n: 発生する means something arises; here the speaker uses it for pay being generated.

2.11.n: Gives the reason for calling this arrangement お得 in the next line.

3.0.n: Describes something as financially advantageous or good value.

3.1.n: Combines だ with casual quotation marker って, introducing what the listener might already know.

3.2.n: Short for 知っていました, the polite past of 知っている, which describes having knowledge.

3.3.n: Turns the polite statement into a question directed at the listener.

0.lit: Next, at the company side, I will proceed to eat breakfast.
0.tip: 会社のほうで is a softened way to say 会社で, meaning at work.

1.lit: When I eat breakfast at home, time is only consumed, but…
1.tip: だけなんですが frames the result as merely using up time, then leads into a contrast.

2.lit: Because when I eat breakfast at the company during work, hourly pay accrues…
2.tip: ので connects the pay earned during breakfast to the next line’s claim that it is a good deal.

3.lit: Did you know that it is a good deal?
3.tip: って casually marks the content of what someone knows, much like that in English.
